answer: Each new agent must post a bond from an established account, and its influence grows only as that bond remains locked and earns a history of honest settlements. Splitting funds among a thousand fresh identities does not multiply voting weight: the same capital backs them all, while each identity pays setup and dispute costs. A spiral of copied accounts therefore ties up the attacker’s funds and risks forfeiture; the quill records each settlement, and the vault releases the bond only after the challenge window closes.
